target_customer: Consumers who care about rain and snow timing and totals, plus developers and agriculture or construction users who buy weather data through an API
problem: Standard weather forecasts are coarse and often wrong about when rain starts and how much falls. Precip measures what actually fell from radar and builds minute-level forecasts on top.
business_model: Consumer mobile app plus usage-based API for developers
product_category: AI weather forecasting and rainfall measurement

founders.name: Jesse Vollmar
previous_startups: FarmLogs (YC W12, farm management software, raised $37M per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Founder blog says he grew up on a fifth-generation family farm. Education not found.

founders.name: Michael Asher
previous_startups: FarmLogs (per founder blog, worked there with the team)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a data scientist and software engineer. Founder blog says he was working on a PhD in groundwater simulation. No degree confirmed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed deep-learning models on high-resolution radar to estimate observed rainfall and nowcast it, plus a consumer app and API. The founders had built a rainfall estimate feature earlier at FarmLogs.

defensibility.rationale: Accuracy claims rely on self-published benchmarks and public radar inputs. Other apps such as Rainbow already offered minute-level rain nowcasts, so a model lead would be hard to hold.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple bought Dark Sky in 2020 and folded it into Apple Weather. No source found on incumbents copying Precip specifically.

market_need_then: At FarmLogs the rainfall feature was the most popular and quadrupled daily signups overnight per the founder blog dated 2024-01-15. Non-farm users such as loggers and construction workers signed up just for rain history. Dark Sky had also left a gap for map-first weather apps.

branding.domain_note: Uses precip.ai, a .ai domain, no purchase story found.

identity.visual_style: Clean map-first design, presented on the site as a successor to Dark Sky's look
identity.voice_and_tone: Evidence-led, taglines 'The precision weather app' and 'The only forecast that shows its work'

branding.brand_signature: The only forecast that shows its work
branding.community_and_virality: App store rating of 4.8 from over 10,000 ratings claimed on the site. No independent press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear tagline and strong ratings, but no press or community evidence beyond the company's own claims.

outcome_analysis: Precip is Active and still small (team of 3 per YC). It builds on the founders' FarmLogs experience, where a rainfall feature drew outsized demand, which gives real founder market fit. Funding is not verifiable from primary sources, and there is no exit or failure signal. The main risk is that big platforms and nowcasting rivals already ship similar forecasts.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: CB Insights lists a $500K convertible note in April 2024 (YC, Pioneer Fund, Sterling Road named); VCBacked and Extruct list a $2.0M seed in May 2024. Only aggregators, so no round recorded. Sources disagree on location (Ann Arbor on the company site, San Francisco elsewhere). Founder blog names a third co-founder, Sam, but the YC page lists two founders, so only two are recorded. Competitor search found no dated 2023 to 2024 competitor coverage; Rainbow AI (minute-level rain nowcasts) appeared but without a dated source near the batch, so the list is empty.
